name: Small inclusion-maximal Sidon sets in [1,256]
description: Construct a Sidon subset of the integer interval [1,256] that cannot be extended by any other interval element, and minimize its cardinality. The verifier checks every unordered pair sum including diagonal pairs and tries every missing element. This is the N=256 instance of the minimal-size maximal-set problem listed as JSP-000154, distinct from the existing maximum-cardinality Sidon-set task.

sources.locator: Imre Z. Ruzsa, A Small Maximal Sidon Set, Ramanujan Journal 2 (1998), pp.55–58. Small inclusion-maximal Sidon sets in [1,N]; local exhaustive verifier and greedy seed do not reproduce Ruzsa's asymptotic construction. Primary publisher abstract and bibliography inspected; full text subscription restricted.

J. A. Dias da Silva and Melvyn B. Nathanson, Maximal Sidon sets and matroids (2009), section 1. Sidon definition includes multisets (repeated elements); the example {1,3,4} is maximal in [1,7] despite a larger Sidon set existing.
JSP-000154: smallest cardinality of inclusion-maximal Sidon sets; N=256 resource-bounded instance chosen locally.

requirements.datasets: No downloaded data; exact finite integer/combinatorial certificates.

evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: construct() -> a nonempty list of distinct Python integers in [1,N]. All unordered sums a+b with a<=b must be distinct INCLUDING a=a. Adding ANY missing integer from [1,N] must destroy this property. Minimize cardinality. Fixed N=256 is a finite adaptation of the small maximal Sidon-set problem; maximal means inclusion-maximal, not maximum cardinality.

provenance.borrowed_component: Mathematical definitions and cited constructive reference in tests only; all evaluator and seed code authored locally

limitations: These are independently implemented finite certificate/search tasks. They are not Lean proofs, prize submissions, full general-conjecture solutions, or claims of eligibility or mathematical novelty.

The prize catalog is a discovery source whose statements and contributor records can change. The pinned revision is recorded; original mathematical authorship is separate from this local implementation.
Candidate Python code is trusted code; the evaluator process is not a security sandbox.
An accepted set establishes feasibility and an upper bound on the minimum cardinality for N=256. It does not prove optimality or resolve the general asymptotic problem.
Repeated-element sums a+a are included. Maximal means no strict Sidon superset in the interval; it does not mean maximum size.
The ascending greedy baseline is local code. No construction coordinates, implementation, or algorithm from Ruzsa's paper are imported.
